News Commentary

CHICAGO, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shareholders in five big-board companies have a raise on the way. Between October 27 and November 17, 2026, the boards of a global payments network, an industrial automation company, an oil and gas producer, a payroll and HR technology provider and a public safety technology company each approved a higher dividend, with increases ranging from 7% to 16%.
Active Companies from around the markets with current developments include: Visa Inc. (
), Emerson Electric Co. (NYSE: EMR), EOG Resources, Inc. (NYSE: EOG), Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (Nasdaq: ADP), Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: MSI)

The five raises came in different ways. Three were announced alongside quarterly or full-year results, while two arrived in standalone dividend announcements after the companies had already reported. The new payouts start reaching shareholders on December 1, 2026, with the last of the five scheduled for January 29, 2027. Taken together, they span payments, automation, energy, workforce software and public safety communications, so the extra income is coming from very different businesses.
Visa Inc. (

raised its quarterly cash dividend 16% to $0.780 per share, up from $0.670, when it reported fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 results on October 27, 2026. The new dividend is payable on December 1, 2026, to all holders of record as of November 10, 2026.

Visa reported fiscal fourth-quarter net revenue of $12.1 billion, an increase of 13% on a nominal and constant-dollar basis, and full-year net revenue of $45.9 billion, an increase of 15%. Total processed transactions in the quarter reached 74.2 billion, up 10% from the prior year, and cross-border volume increased 14% on a constant-dollar basis. Share repurchases and dividends totaled $5.2 billion for the fiscal fourth quarter and $25.6 billion for the full year, and Visa had $24.4 billion of remaining authorized funds for share repurchases as of September 30, 2026.
Emerson Electric Co. (NYSE: EMR)

declared a 7% increase in its quarterly cash dividend to $0.595 per share of common stock, up from $0.555, as it reported fourth quarter and full year 2026 results on November 4, 2026. The higher dividend is payable December 10, 2026, to stockholders of record November 13, 2026.

For the fourth quarter, Emerson reported underlying orders up 14%, net sales up 7% to $5.201 billion from $4.855 billion, and adjusted earnings per share up 15% to $1.86. Full-year free cash flow rose 9% to $3.535 billion. Emerson also provided its initial fiscal 2027 outlook, with guidance for adjusted earnings per share of about $7.25, and a framework that assumes returning about $3.8 billion through about $2.5 billion of share repurchases and about $1.3 billion of dividends.
EOG Resources, Inc. (NYSE: EOG)

raised its regular quarterly dividend 8% to $1.10 per share, a $4.40 per share indicated annual rate, in its third quarter 2026 results announced on November 5, 2026. The prior regular dividend was $1.02 per share. The new dividend will be payable January 29, 2027, to stockholders of record as of January 15, 2027, and the company noted that it has paid a regular dividend for 28 straight years.

EOG reported third quarter net income of $2.8 billion, or $5.33 per share, and adjusted net income of $2.5 billion, or $4.87 per share. The company generated $2.2 billion of free cash flow, paid $544 million in regular dividends and repurchased $1.0 billion of shares. EOG also reported record oil, NGL and natural gas volumes, all better than guidance midpoints, and entered a new long-term gas sales agreement linked to JKM pricing starting by 2030.
Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (Nasdaq: ADP)

announced on November 11, 2026, that its board of directors approved a $0.20 increase in the quarterly cash dividend, bringing the quarterly rate to $1.90 per share and the annual rate to $7.60 per share. The company said the increase marks the 52nd consecutive year in which ADP has raised its quarterly dividend. The new quarterly rate will be distributed on January 1, 2027, to shareholders of record on December 11, 2026. President and Chief Executive Officer Maria Black called it a 12% increase and tied it to the board's confidence in ADP's financial strength.

ADP, which describes itself as a global leader in HR and payroll solutions, says more than 1.1 million clients across 140+ countries rely on its service. On October 28, 2026, the company reported first quarter fiscal 2027 results, with revenues up 6% to $5.5 billion, or 6% on an organic constant currency basis, and adjusted diluted EPS up 13% to $2.82. ADP also raised its full year guidance, now expecting fiscal 2027 revenue growth of about 6%, up from its prior outlook of 5% to 6%, and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 10% to 12%, up from 9% to 11%.
Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: MSI)

announced on November 17, 2026, that its board of directors had increased its regular quarterly dividend by 11 percent to $1.34 per share, up from $1.21. The next quarterly dividend will be payable in cash on January 15, 2027, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 15, 2026.

The raise followed the company's third quarter 2026 results on November 4, 2026, when Motorola Solutions reported sales of $3.4 billion, up 12% versus a year ago, and a record ending backlog of $16.6 billion, up 14%, driven by record third quarter orders. The company raised its full-year revenue and earnings outlook again, now expecting revenue of approximately $13.050 billion, up from its prior guidance of $12.975 billion, and non-GAAP EPS between $17.94 and $17.99 per share. It also announced a $2 billion increase to its share repurchase authorization and highlighted a $140 million P25 systems and device order with the Federal Bureau of Prisons.

For shareholders, the calendar now fills in nicely: Visa's higher dividend is payable December 1, Emerson's on December 10, ADP's on January 1, Motorola Solutions' on January 15 and EOG's on January 29. From Emerson's 7% to Visa's 16%, five companies have now lined up more cash for shareholders through the turn of the year.
